author: mvafin
title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus invalid-pch error on shared cmake_pch.hxx.gch
signature: cc1plus: error: cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API step fails: dozens of cc1plus invocations in src/core/reference report cmake_pch.hxx.gch is not a PCH file, escalated to an error by -Werror=invalid-pch

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status job exits failure because the Build job failed

root_cause: During the ARM64 cross-compilation build, 13+ translation units in the openvino_reference CMake target failed to compile because the precompiled header cmake_pch.hxx.gch consumed by cc1plus is not recognized as a valid PCH file. Because CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR is enabled, the 'not a PCH file' diagnostic is escalated by -Werror=invalid-pch into a hard ninja build failure. The commit under investigation (#38602) only changes ONNX frontend Dropout training_mode handling (src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op/dropout.cpp and its test) - it does not touch src/core/reference, PCH generation, or cmake/toolchain configuration, so the failure is unrelated to this PR's diff. This is now the 3rd recorded occurrence of the identical signature (first seen 2026-09-25 in openvino_shape_inference, 2nd seen 2026-10-06 00:24 also in openvino_reference, both on unrelated PRs), confirming a recurring build-environment/toolchain issue rather than a source regression: most likely a stale or partially-written .gch artifact being reused across build/cache restores (sccache + CMake PCH interaction) instead of being regenerated before consumption, possibly exacerbated by parallel ninja jobs racing on the same PCH compile unit.
reproduction_steps: Not directly reproducible from a clean checkout without the exact runner image/cache state. To attempt reproduction: use the ARM64 cross-compilation Docker image referenced by this workflow, configure with the same cmake options (-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/arm64.toolchain.cmake, CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON, CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache), restore a prior build-directory/sccache cache, then run a parallel ninja build and check whether src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch is cleanly regenerated before being consumed by dependent .cpp.o compiles.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Linux (Ubuntu 22.04, ARM64 cross-compilation, Python 3.11)' workflow; this is the 3rd occurrence of the same signature on unrelated PRs, so a rerun is very likely to pass.

Escalate to infra/build-tooling owners: this signature has now recurred 3 times across different targets (openvino_shape_inference, openvino_reference twice) - prioritize root-causing the PCH/sccache cache interaction rather than treating each occurrence as independent flakiness.

Investigate whether sccache is caching/restoring PCH-related compiler invocations (CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache combined with CMake PCH) across build directories/containers for the ARM64 cross-compilation job, and whether a partially-written or stale .gch from a previous run is reused instead of regenerated.

Consider excluding PCH object files (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) from any build-directory/sccache cache restored between runs for this job, or add an explicit freshness check (checksum/timestamp of .gch vs its source header) before the compile step consumes it.

As a stopgap, consider not escalating -Werror=invalid-pch to a hard failure for PCH-consuming targets on this cross-compilation configuration until the underlying cache/race is fixed, since a stale PCH should trigger a full regeneration rather than fail the whole build.
prevention_strategies: Ensure PCH artifacts (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) are always freshly generated per build and are never restored from a cross-run build-directory or sccache cache for the ARM64 cross-compilation job. Add a CI step that verifies PCH freshness before the compile step consumes it, so a stale artifact triggers a clean rebuild instead of a hard failure. Given this is a 3rd recurrence, treat it as a tracked infra defect rather than ad-hoc flakiness.
historical_context: Exact same signature recorded twice before: 2026-09-25 (run 36123294303, PR #38393, failed in openvino_shape_inference) and 2026-10-06 00:24 (run 37391757947, PR #38483, failed in openvino_reference). All three occurrences are on PRs whose diffs are unrelated to src/core/reference, PCH generation, or cmake/toolchain configuration, confirming this is a recurring (now 3x) build-environment/cache issue in the post-commit knowledge base, not a code regression.
